reason: Cancellate means latticed, marked with a net of crossing lines or ridges, as on achene and nutlet surfaces; that is the reviewed FLOPO reticulate. 'Cancellinae' (hyaline leaf cells of Calymperaceae) is a cell, not this quality.

label: paroicous
definition: A phenotypic sex quality inhering in a bryophyte by virtue of its antheridia and archegonia being borne in the same inflorescence, the antheridia naked in the axils of leaves below the archegonia.
reason: Bryophyte sexual condition with no PATO term; sibling of FLOPO:0991093 autoicous, where the antheridia are in a separate inflorescence on the same plant.

target: cystolith (no PO class; FLOPO anatomy class needed) present
reason: 'Covered with cystoliths' states the presence of cystoliths, calcium carbonate concretions in leaf cells, which is a part and not a quality. PO has no cystolith, so a FLOPO anatomy class must be added first (as was done for glochid).

label: prorate
definition: A surface feature shape quality inhering in a cell by virtue of one or both of its ends projecting above the surface of the structure it lies in, as a papilla-like bump.
reason: A standard moss term for laminal cells whose ends project. It differs from FLOPO:0991059 papillose, where the papillae stand over the cell body and not at the cell ends.
Rimose means marked with cracks; FLOPO fissured covers bark and axes cracked into clefts and has 'cracked' as a synonym.
A compound of two shape values, PATO:0001954 subulate and lanceolate, like 'linear-lanceolate'; it is handled as a continuum between the two values, not as a new term.
'Sub-' is the approximate qualifier on FLOPO:0991046 membranous, the same as 'suborbicular' in pattern 01.

Near the middle: approximately PATO:0002268 centered. The bearers are mixed (sori between costa and margin, a nearly central midvein, anthers fixed near the middle), so there is no single new value to coin.
Negation of the reviewed FLOPO crisped.
A translation of French 'soudés'. 'Sepals, petals or filaments soudés à la base' means like parts united, which is FLOPO connate (as the rule for 'united').
The complement of 'lenticellate' (lenticel present): branches without lenticels.

label: urticating
definition: A structural quality inhering in a trichome by virtue of its being a stiff hair with a brittle tip that breaks on contact and injects an irritant into the skin; said of a plant or part that bears such hairs.
reason: Stinging hairs (Urticaceae, Mucuna fruits, Tragia) have no PATO or PO term. For a whole plant or organ the word means it bears such hairs.

label: root-climbing
definition: A climbing quality inhering in a plant by virtue of its clinging to its support by adventitious roots arising along the stem.
reason: A well-defined kind of climbing habit (Hedera, many Araceae and Marcgraviaceae); a child of FLOPO climbing keeps the information that plain 'climbing' would lose.

label: pseudoterminal
definition: A positional quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's appearing terminal on a shoot although it arises laterally, in the axil of the uppermost leaf, the shoot apex being arrested or displaced to one side.
reason: Common in inflorescence descriptions and distinct from PATO:0002476 terminal, which it only seems to be.

'Pétales internes', 'tepals les internes', '6 stamens internes' name the inner members of a series, a series position of the bearer (as 'inner tepal' became tepal plus position). The inner position value is among those proposed for the next release.

Vesiculose means made of or covered with bladder-like, inflated cells (moss annulus cells, seed-coat cells). PATO inflated is the nearest existing quality; the seed-surface use may later need a surface-feature value.
'Peristome or palea fully developed' contrasts with reduced or rudimentary, which earlier rules map to PATO vestigial; the statement is its negation.
Obloid is the solid form of oblong. PATO oblong is defined as elongated with approximately parallel sides and is not restricted to 2-D outlines.

label: limbate
definition: A structural quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's margin being bordered by a distinct band of differentiated, usually elongate and thick-walled cells.
reason: A bryological term (Fissidens laminae) with no PATO or PO term. The French uses ('munies d'un limbe' = with a blade) mean leaf lamina present and should not be given this class.
French 'many-flowered' is an inexact count of flowers per inflorescence or head.
The colour green inheres in the apex of the phyllary, bract or lobe, so it is the part-of-the-bearer pattern with a PATO green value, not a new term.
Exauriculate means without auricles, the negation of PATO auriculate. The bearers (pinnule bases, leaf bases, claws) are not grass leaf sheaths, so PO_0020106 does not fit.
'Distal stem leaves bracteal' means leaves reduced and resembling bracts, which is FLOPO bract-like.
PATO caudate is defined as having a tail or tail-like projection; 'not tailed' is its negation.

label: decompound
definition: A structural quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being compound or branched more than once, its primary divisions being themselves divided.
reason: Used for leaves and inflorescences without saying the mode of division. It is broader than FLOPO:0991014 bipinnate and FLOPO:0991159 tripinnate, which are its specific cases.

label: polycarpic
definition: A reproductive quality inhering in a plant by virtue of its flowering and fruiting repeatedly during its life, without dying after the first fruiting.
reason: Not the same as PATO_0104361 perennial life span, because there are monocarpic perennials (Agave, many bamboos). PATO has no iteroparity quality.

label: complanate-foliate
definition: A spatial pattern quality inhering in a shoot by virtue of its leaves spreading in one plane, so that the leafy shoot appears flattened.
reason: A standard moss term. PATO_0002254 flattened would wrongly say the stem itself is flat; here the flattening comes from how the leaves are arranged.
An inexact count of leaves on a stem or inflorescence, like 'few-flowered'.
The quality is FLOPO sheathing. 'Long' is the length of the sheath and could be added as a second statement on the sheath, but it does not need a term.

label: helicoid
definition: A coiled quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's successive branches arising always on the same side, so that the axis is coiled in a helix out of one plane.
reason: The helicoid cyme (bostryx) is the counterpart of the reviewed FLOPO:0991179 scorpioid, which is coiled in one plane; PATO has no helix-shaped coiled quality.
